reviews.body: No objections. Still, the receiverless each feels wrong . I’d rather used explicit. Tell us more about your case

review_comments.body:
Nitpick: why not just next unless node.receiver?
Isn’t there a cop for this? Why it’s not offended?

comments.body:
@pirj

Pushed `9e2830d4a`: `next unless node.receiver` instead of `next if node.receiver.nil?`. There's no `receiver?` predicate on the node — only `receiver` (returns the node or `nil`) — so this is the equivalent, idiomatic form. `bundle exec rake` still green (2471/2471, 100% line+branch), self-lint clean.

On the cop: checked. `bundle exec rubocop lib/rubocop/cop/rspec/iterated_expectation.rb` and `rake internal_investigation` (293 files) both report no offenses for either form, before or after the change. Nothing in this repo's `.rubocop.yml` currently flags `if x.nil?` in favor of `unless x`.

On the case: there isn't a real-world spec behind this one. `each?`'s pattern is `(send ... :each)` — the `...` matches any number of children, so it accepts a receiverless call the same as an explicit one. I was checking the cop's node patterns against syntax they'd match but the code didn't anticipate, the same way #2214 came from feeding it `itblock`/`numblock` shapes. `receiver.source` assumed a receiver always exists; a bare `each { |x| ... }` is enough to prove it doesn't.

Agreed the shape reads oddly — RuboCop only sees the AST, so it doesn't know whether `self` (the example) actually responds to `each` at runtime; it just matches the send pattern and then crashes trying to read a receiver that isn't there. The fix doesn't require the call to be realistic, only that the cop not crash before deciding whether to flag it.

I’m more inclined to close this.
Happy to re-open if this fixes a real life issue.

@pirj Understood — closing on my end too. You've got a fair read: crash-fixing an AST shape that doesn't correspond to real code is a defensible thing to skip carrying, especially with two more of these open right now asking the same question. Appreciate you taking the time to look at it either way.
